data.narrative:
Mission Zero Technologies is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised £21.8M to date. The valuation universe comprises nine peers in the climate and energy sector, including eight private companies (Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen among them) and one public comparable, Lanzatech (LNZA).

Standard peer-median triangulation is not applicable here. The climate and energy sector lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables to support a reliable multiple-based valuation. A search for peers at Mission Zero's stage or within adjacent funding rounds and similar valuation tiers yielded fewer than three datapoints, the minimum threshold for meaningful median analysis. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial noise given the heterogeneity of business models, technology maturity, and market dynamics within climate tech.

In the absence of a statistically robust peer set, valuation analysis must rely on method diversification—venture capital method modeling, comparable transaction analysis, or discounted cash flow approaches informed by the broader peer universe. The public comparable (LNZA) and late-stage private peers provide directional reference but do not eliminate the fundamental challenge: early-stage climate tech valuations remain highly sensitive to technology risk, regulatory assumptions, and capital intensity, none of which can be reliably anchored to peer multiples. Further data collection on recent Series A financings in narrow subsectors would be required to triangulate a defensible range.
